answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and holds one shard on an island store, listed on the garden board under a shard-to-key seal. Each epoch a zephyr sweep picks a random shard and byte offset; it must return signed bytes, or a wrong answer burns the bond and sinks the 15-credit fee. The thousandth fake needs its own shard, bond, and fee, so 1,000 fakes risk 85,000 credits: one seal covers one shard only. To forge a custody proof fails: the offset is unknown beforehand, so no fabrication matches them. An honest operator holds one shard, pays one fee, and recovers the bond after one epoch.
